title: Google Acquires Crusoe's Troubled Wyoming Data Center
summary: Google takes over Crusoe's unfinished Wyoming data center project after cost and timeline concerns, investing $17 billion to complete the facility.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 6, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Google acquired Crusoe's unfinished Wyoming data center after raising concerns about escalating costs and construction delays under the developer's management.
- The tech giant will invest $17 billion to complete the facility originally planned for 10 gigawatts capacity, highlighting challenges independent developers face.
- Despite the Wyoming setback, Google continues working with Crusoe on a separate Texas data center project while Crusoe maintains major contracts with Oracle, OpenAI, and Microsoft.


Google has acquired an incomplete data center project in southeastern Wyoming from Crusoe Energy, taking direct control after the Denver-based developer encountered significant cost overruns and construction delays. Officially announced on November 6, 2026, the deal marks a rare instance of a major tech company stepping in to salvage a third-party infrastructure project that failed to meet expectations.


## Why Google Took Over the Project


Crusoe, recently valued at $30.9 billion, originally planned the Wyoming facility with Blackstone-backed infrastructure firm Tallgrass, targeting an eventual 10 gigawatts of power capacity. Google, initially approached as a potential customer for the site, reportedly raised concerns about escalating costs and missed construction milestones under Crusoe's management. Rather than walk away entirely, Google chose to acquire the unfinished project and inject $17 billion to complete the development.


The financial terms of the acquisition remain undisclosed, but the takeover underscores the mounting challenges independent data center developers face in delivering hyperscale projects. Securing sufficient power capacity, procuring specialized equipment, and navigating local opposition have become critical bottlenecks in the AI infrastructure race.


## Release Date and Deal Timeline


Officially announced on November 6, 2026, the Wyoming acquisition follows months of negotiations. Bloomberg first reported the pending sale in June 2026, though Crusoe continued to secure funding despite the setback, closing a $3.9 billion financing round in September 2026.


## Crusoe's Broader AI Infrastructure Portfolio


The Wyoming sale has not severed the Google-Crusoe relationship entirely. Crusoe continues developing a separate data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. Beyond Google, Crusoe maintains a robust customer roster across the AI industry:


- Its Abilene, Texas campus serves Oracle and OpenAI, with phased construction ongoing
- A separate 900-megawatt campus next door hosts Microsoft, with the first building expected online by mid-2027
- Meta remains an active customer, and Bloomberg reported a $13 billion, five-year cloud deal with trading firm Jane Street


Crusoe generates revenue through three channels: leasing data center space to customers who bring their own GPUs, renting its own GPU inventory, and selling inference compute power for running AI models. The company was founded by CEO Chase Lochmiller and Cully Cavness as a cryptocurrency mining operation powered by natural gas that would otherwise be flared.


## Independent Developer Challenges


The Wyoming project highlights systemic difficulties facing data center developers attempting to meet the infrastructure demands of generative AI. Hyperscale facilities require not only massive capital but also reliable access to power grids, specialized cooling systems, and advanced networking equipment, all of which face global supply constraints. Local community pushback over environmental impact and grid strain adds another layer of complexity.


Crusoe's September 2026 funding round, which brought three new board members including Tesla board member and Redwood Materials founder JB Straubel, demonstrated continued investor confidence despite the Wyoming setback. Straubel had previously invested in Crusoe in 2021, and Crusoe later became the first customer of his energy storage business.


## What This Means


Google's decision to acquire rather than abandon the Wyoming site signals the urgency major tech companies feel in securing AI compute infrastructure. With data center capacity emerging as a strategic constraint on model development and deployment, vertical integration into facility ownership may become more common. For independent developers like Crusoe, the episode underscores the execution risk inherent in competing for hyperscale contracts against customers who possess the capital and expertise to take projects in-house.
